_comment: Hand-written rows and the height basis each must get. Read by frontend/lib/heightBasis.test.mts (heightBasis) and pipeline/tests/test_daily_report_height_basis.py (daily_report.height_basis), so the page and the report prompt cannot label the same row differently. Every expected value is written out here, never computed by the code under test. face_ft is face_ft_raw divided by the spot's factor and rounded to 2 dp, exactly as face_correction.apply_face_corrections writes it; the arithmetic is in each case's note.

cases.name: calibrated, factor above 1 (steamer-lane-like, 2.0)
cases.note: 4.62 / 2.0 = 2.31: the published height is the smaller one

cases.name: calibrated, factor BELOW 1 (point-arena, 0.9313)
cases.note: 3.1 / 0.9313 = 3.3287 -> 3.33: the published height is LARGER than the raw one, so a raw > face test would call this a model estimate

cases.name: calibrated, on the WW3 path the NWPS override did not cover
cases.note: the correction divides every rated hour of a calibrated spot, whichever producer wrote it: 3.8 / 2.0 = 1.9

cases.name: a MOP-tier spot's model row (the hours readers see there)
cases.note: MOP-tier spots are never corrected (face_correction.MOP_TIER_SOURCES), so raw equals face; the hour is not MOP-fed

cases.name: a MOP-tier spot's model row on the NWPS fallback
cases.note: rate_spot's NWPS fallback; not MOP-fed, not corrected

cases.name: a MOP-fed row
cases.note: apply_mop_overrides writes MOP Hs x 3.281 and tags the hour cdip_mop; the correction skips the tier

cases.name: uncalibrated NWPS spot
cases.note: no factor: stamp_provenance copied face into raw and nothing divided

cases.name: uncalibrated NWPS spot, DIRPW direction
cases.note: the NWPS override's fallback tag is 'nwps', which is not 'cdip_mop'

cases.name: row written before migration 017
cases.note: no raw value is no evidence of calibration; the label must not claim it

cases.name: flat hour at a calibrated spot
cases.note: 0 / factor = 0: dividing changed nothing, and the number shown is exactly the model's

cases.name: swell_source missing
cases.note: nothing says CDIP, so it is not called CDIP

cases.name: a near miss on the MOP tag
cases.note: the tag is matched exactly; a looser match is how a model row gets called CDIP's

cases.name: unrateable hour
cases.note: no height, so nothing to label

cases.name: calibrated AND tagged cdip_mop (cannot happen: the MOP tier is never corrected)
cases.note: the order the rule is stated in: a divided height is not CDIP's own any more
